js_control.title: Write event-driven JavaScript controls
js_control.explanation: Open Options for the JavaScript editor. Define named numeric inputs and outputs, bind MIDI, OSC, metronome or named controls, then Check and Apply while the engine runs. MIDI passthrough (on by default) relays incoming MIDI to the MIDI output unchanged while the script reads it, and merges anything the script sends into that stream; turn it off when the script should consume incoming MIDI. The Scripting guide in Options and Help contains the full API, examples, timing semantics and resource limits. JavaScript runs outside audio rendering with asynchronous response latency.
steps: Add JavaScript control and open Options.
Choose an example or write define_input and define_output declarations, then Apply script.
Connect its named numeric ports or MIDI port and enable the engine. Open Console to view console.log messages.
Read Help → JavaScript scripting for the complete event and helper reference.

add.title: Transpose a melody
add.explanation: Add 12 semitones to MIDI note 60: the display becomes 72, one octave higher.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

subtract.title: Measure pitch distance
subtract.explanation: Subtract root note 60 from note 67 to obtain a seven-semitone interval.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

multiply.title: Scale note velocity
multiply.explanation: Multiply a MIDI velocity of 100 by 0.5 to obtain 50 for a quieter layer.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

divide.title: Normalize MIDI velocity
divide.explanation: Divide velocity 100 by 127 to obtain a 0–1 amplitude control (about 0.787).
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

modulo.title: Wrap a four-step index
modulo.explanation: Modulo wraps counter value 7 to index 3. Use it to cycle through a shorter phrase.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

power.title: Shape a fader response
power.explanation: Square a normalized fader value: 0.5 becomes 0.25, giving more travel at quiet levels.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

min.title: Cap modulation depth
min.explanation: Choose the smaller input so a performer cannot request more than 0.6 modulation depth.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

max.title: Keep a minimum level

steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

greater.title: Detect loud playing
greater.explanation: Velocity 100 exceeds the threshold 80, producing 1. A quieter note produces 0.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

less.title: Detect a quiet passage
less.explanation: Velocity 25 is below 40, producing 1 for a quiet-passage condition.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

equal.title: Recognize a beat index
equal.explanation: Matching integer step indices produce 1. Use integer values when testing exact equality.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

and.explanation: A performer-ready control and a conductor-ready control must both be nonzero to output 1.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

or.title: Accept either cue
or.explanation: Either of two cue switches can enable the shared condition.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

abs.title: Measure bipolar depth
abs.explanation: Turn −0.75 into magnitude 0.75 without retaining the modulation direction.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

sqrt.title: Soften a response curve
sqrt.explanation: Square root maps 0.25 to 0.5. Keep inputs nonnegative for this curve.

steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

cos.explanation: Cosine starts at 1 for phase 0, a quarter-cycle offset from sine.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

log.title: Inspect a ratio logarithm
log.explanation: Natural logarithm maps a positive ratio near e to 1. Zero and negative inputs have no real logarithm.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

exp.explanation: Exponentiation maps 1 to e (about 2.718). Limit the input before using this as a gain control.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

not.title: Invert a mute condition
not.explanation: Zero becomes 1; any nonzero numeric condition becomes 0.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

mtof.title: Tune an oscillator from notes
mtof.explanation: MIDI note 69 becomes 440 Hz. This conversion connects note-valued controls to oscillator Frequency.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

ftom.title: Read frequency as a note
ftom.explanation: 440 Hz becomes MIDI note 69. This is a numeric conversion, not audio pitch detection.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

dbtoa.title: Convert a level to amplitude
dbtoa.explanation: −6 dB becomes approximately 0.501 amplitude. Use amplitude-valued instrument controls as destinations.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

atodb.title: Read an envelope in decibels
atodb.explanation: Amplitude 0.5 becomes about −6.02 dB. This also adapts an ADSR’s linear output to Gain’s dB parameter.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

clamp.title: Constrain a normalized control
clamp.explanation: Clamp the input to 0–1: 1.4 becomes 1. Put it after a range mapping when extrapolation is unwanted.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

scale.title: Map a fader to decibels
scale.explanation: Map 0–1 to −60–0 dB. The halfway fader value becomes −30 dB; values outside the input range extrapolate.
steps: Edit Input value and the documented node’s parameters in their modals. Enable the engine to observe the result in a real project.

clock.title: Count an eight-pulse phrase
clock.explanation: The counter advances on rising pulses and wraps after 7. The graph clock runs with the engine; show Play realigns project clocks to the score. An independent Metronome has its own BPM.
steps: Console Out is read in Settings → Console; control displays show sampled telemetry, so brief pulses may be easier to count with a Counter.

select.explanation: Select emits a trigger when the counter reaches 3 (the fourth zero-based step). Watch that cue separately from the running count.
steps: Console Out is read in Settings → Console; control displays show sampled telemetry, so brief pulses may be easier to count with a Counter.

change.title: Count changed step values
change.explanation: Change turns each new counter value into a one-sample pulse. It is useful when a downstream action should happen only as a value changes.

trigger.title: Count an eight-pulse phrase
trigger.explanation: Click Trigger to advance an eight-step counter once. A pulse returns to zero after one engine sample, ready for the next click.
steps: Console Out is read in Settings → Console; control displays show sampled telemetry, so brief pulses may be easier to count with a Counter.

control_delay.title: Offset a rhythm by 125 ms
control_delay.explanation: Delay the eighth-note pulse by 125 ms to make a second rhythmic voice. The delay is in milliseconds, so it does not automatically follow tempo changes.
steps: Console Out is read in Settings → Console; control displays show sampled telemetry, so brief pulses may be easier to count with a Counter.

random.title: Repeatable random choices
random.explanation: Each eighth-note pulse chooses a seeded random value below 8. The fixed seed makes the sequence repeatable when the node is freshly prepared.
steps: Console Out is read in Settings → Console; control displays show sampled telemetry, so brief pulses may be easier to count with a Counter.

step_sequencer.title: Program a four-note ostinato
step_sequencer.explanation: Eighth-note pulses advance C–E–G–C. MIDI to frequency tunes the continuous oscillator; add an ADSR if you want articulated notes.

adsr.title: Build an expressive plucked instrument
adsr.explanation: Piano pitch tunes the oscillator through MIDI to frequency. Note-on and note-off pulses attack and release the ADSR, whose 0–1 output controls oscillator Amplitude directly. This voice is monophonic: play one note at a time. Gain takes decibels, so use Amplitude to dB before driving a Gain node instead.
steps: Try attack 5 ms, decay 180 ms, sustain 0.35 and release 350 ms. Enable the engine, connect the headphone mix, then play and release keys.

piano.title: Audition an instrument without a score
piano.explanation: The typed MIDI cable carries note identity, velocity and releases together. Play a chord and release individual keys; each note releases its own voice. Internal instruments also follow MIDI pitch bend (±2 semitones).

part_midi.title: Orchestrate one score part
part_midi.explanation: The typed MIDI cable carries note identity, velocity and releases together. Play a chord and release individual keys; each note releases its own voice. Internal instruments also follow MIDI pitch bend (±2 semitones).
steps: Create a score part, enter notes and select that part in Part MIDI. Play starts score events; enabling the engine alone does not play the score.

midi_input.title: Play from the server’s MIDI keyboard
midi_input.explanation: The typed MIDI cable carries note identity, velocity and releases together. Play a chord and release individual keys; each note releases its own voice. Internal instruments also follow MIDI pitch bend (±2 semitones).
steps: MIDI input: select the physical MIDI port on the server in the modal. The external instrument needs its own audio return if you want to hear it in this patch.

local_midi_input.title: Play from a client’s MIDI keyboard
local_midi_input.explanation: The typed MIDI cable carries note identity, velocity and releases together. Play a chord and release individual keys; each note releases its own voice. Internal instruments also follow MIDI pitch bend (±2 semitones).
steps: Choose and authorize a MIDI device on this client. Keep this browser/app session connected.

osc_to_midi.title: Play an internal voice from OSC
osc_to_midi.explanation: An external OSC sender supplies pitch and velocity integer pairs; velocity zero releases. The converter feeds typed MIDI into the internal instrument.
steps: Enable the relevant OSC receive/send binding in System settings. Set matching OSC addresses and the receiver host:port in node options; external delivery is best effort.

synth.title: Play a polyphonic sine voice
synth.explanation: The typed MIDI cable carries note identity, velocity and releases together. Play a chord and release individual keys; each note releases its own voice. Internal instruments also follow MIDI pitch bend (±2 semitones).

fm_synth.title: Play a bell-like FM voice
fm_synth.explanation: The typed MIDI cable carries note identity, velocity and releases together. Play a chord and release individual keys; each note releases its own voice. Internal instruments also follow MIDI pitch bend (±2 semitones). A finite decay gives the voice a struck, bell-like contour.

poly_sampler.title: Play a recorded instrument chromatically
poly_sampler.explanation: The typed MIDI cable carries note identity, velocity and releases together. Play a chord and release individual keys; each note releases its own voice. Internal instruments also follow MIDI pitch bend (±2 semitones). Each note has its own ADSR envelope. The sampler reuses the standalone ADSR node’s stage behavior and graph editor; edit Attack, Decay, Sustain and Release in Options, or drag the graph handles. The on-node graph shows the shape and the highest active voice envelope.
steps: Polyphonic sampler: import or choose a project sample in the modal; sample IDs are specific to your server. Set the sample root note for pitched instruments.

For a compact sample palette, add a Sample selector, build its shortlist in options, and connect its Sample ID output to this node’s Sample ID input. Match channel counts; changing the sample stops old playback/voices. The sampler root note remains its configured setting.

Set Attack to 20 ms, Decay to 150 ms, Sustain to 0.6 and Release to 400 ms. Play overlapping notes: each starts its own attack and releases independently. Repeated pitches get separate voices; note-off releases the oldest held matching pitch.

Enable Loop while held for sustained notes longer than the sample. Without looping, playback still ends at the sample boundary. Existing graphs default to Attack 0, Decay 0, Sustain 1 and Release 80 ms. Connected envelope parameters show live engine values and lock the corresponding editor handles.

granular_synth.title: Play a cloud from a field recording
granular_synth.explanation: The typed MIDI cable carries note identity, velocity and releases together. Play a chord and release individual keys; each note releases its own voice. Internal instruments also follow MIDI pitch bend (±2 semitones). Choose a sustained field recording; scan Position while holding a note and widen Spray to scatter grain starts.
steps: Granular synth: import or choose a project sample in the modal; sample IDs are specific to your server. Set the sample root note for pitched instruments.

For a compact sample palette, add a Sample selector, build its shortlist in options, and connect its Sample ID output to this node’s Sample ID input. Match channel counts; changing the sample stops old playback/voices. The sampler root note remains its configured setting.

midi_output.title: Play an external hardware instrument
midi_output.explanation: The typed MIDI cable carries note identity, velocity and releases together. Play a chord and release individual keys; each note releases its own voice. Internal instruments also follow MIDI pitch bend (±2 semitones).
steps: MIDI output: select the physical MIDI port on the server in the modal. The external instrument needs its own audio return if you want to hear it in this patch.

midi_to_osc.title: Send keyboard notes to an OSC instrument
midi_to_osc.explanation: Keyboard note-on/off messages become OSC pitch and velocity integers at the configured destination. Velocity zero releases the pitch; the receiver supplies the sound.
steps: Enable the relevant OSC receive/send binding in System settings. Set matching OSC addresses and the receiver host:port in node options; external delivery is best effort.

drum_pads.title: Trigger a dedicated kick voice
drum_pads.explanation: Bass drum emits a velocity-valued trigger. Connect it to a one-shot FM voice’s Trigger; its finite Decay ends the sound without a held gate. Use the other pad outlets for separate snare, tom and cymbal voices.

midi_to_control.title: Decode one drum note
midi_to_control.explanation: Filter Number to 36 and leave Message type at 0. Note on drives a kick voice; Value supplies velocity. Leaving type unrestricted allows both note attacks and releases to be decoded. Set the Piano starting octave to 2 to play C2 (36).

lfo.title: Sweep a sustained filter
lfo.explanation: A slow sine moves cutoff between 300 and 2000 Hz on a sawtooth voice. Frequency stays in a useful audible range.

knobs.title: Perform a filter sweep with a knob
knobs.explanation: Knob 1 supplies 0–1; Scale maps it to 300–2000 Hz. Connect Local MIDI input to Knobs for MIDI Learn when using a physical controller.

sliders.title: Perform a filter sweep with a fader
sliders.explanation: The default fader range is 0–1; Scale maps it to 300–2000 Hz. A connected slider input becomes read-only and follows its source.

control_input.title: Enter a filter frequency
control_input.explanation: Enter 1000 in the graphical numeric control to set filter cutoff in Hz. Connected graphical controls display their engine source instead of accepting manual edits. A Step in Options snaps slider dragging and the arrow keys/buttons of Integer, Float and Slider controls to that increment; 0 keeps the defaults.

value.title: Recall a fixed filter frequency
value.explanation: Set value stores 1000 Hz. With Trigger disconnected it outputs continuously; add a trigger to recall the stored value on a cue.

ramp.title: Smooth a filter movement
ramp.explanation: Slew toward the moving cutoff target over 600 ms, rounding abrupt control movements. The time is a control slew, not an audio delay.

gate.title: Enable or hold a modulation route
gate.explanation: Toggle controls whether the LFO passes. A closed gate outputs zero; the filter clamps that value to its minimum cutoff. Use Audio gate to silence the audio itself.

toggle.title: Mute and unmute a voice
toggle.explanation: The latched switch drives Audio gate Open: checked passes the voice, cleared silences it. Manual state is saved; engine-driven state is transient.

sample_hold.title: Step a smooth modulation on the beat
sample_hold.explanation: The LFO moves continuously but Sample & hold captures it only on a clock pulse, producing stepped filter settings.

osc_input.title: Receive a normalized filter control
osc_input.explanation: Send one number in the 0–1 range at the configured OSC address. Scale converts it to filter Hz; text mode must be off.
steps: Enable the relevant OSC receive/send binding in System settings. Set matching OSC addresses and the receiver host:port in node options; external delivery is best effort.

osc_output.title: Send a moving filter value to another application
osc_output.explanation: An LFO sends a 300–2000 value range to an external filter over OSC. Set its address to the parameter expected by the receiver and choose a sensible send-rate limit.
steps: Enable the relevant OSC receive/send binding in System settings. Set matching OSC addresses and the receiver host:port in node options; external delivery is best effort.

lowpass.title: Warm a bright saw voice
lowpass.explanation: Remove upper harmonics from a sawtooth voice. Lower Cutoff for warmth; higher pole counts make the rolloff steeper.

highpass.title: Remove microphone rumble
highpass.explanation: Cut low-frequency handling noise from a microphone before it enters the headphone mix.
steps: Source: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

bandpass.title: Make a telephone voice
bandpass.explanation: Focus a microphone around the speech midrange. Q controls how narrow the band becomes.
steps: Source: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

notch.title: Reduce a narrow hum component
notch.explanation: Reject a narrow 60 Hz band from the input. Other hum harmonics need separate notches; this does not remove broadband noise.
steps: Source: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

eq3.title: Shape a vocal tone
eq3.explanation: Trim bass, add midrange presence and soften the top using three independently adjustable peaking bands.
steps: Source: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

eq5.title: Carve space for an instrument
eq5.explanation: Cut the 300 Hz band to reduce muddiness and lift 3500 Hz for articulation. Adjust frequency and Q to suit the source.
steps: Source: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

compressor.title: Control vocal dynamics
compressor.explanation: Compress loud microphone passages. With Sidechain disconnected, the processor detects its own input; connect a different audio source for ducking.
steps: Source: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

noise_gate.title: Close a microphone between phrases
noise_gate.explanation: Use the input’s own detector to attenuate low-level background sound between phrases. Set threshold below the quietest wanted phrase.
steps: Source: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

expander.title: Gently reduce room noise
expander.explanation: Expand the level range so quiet microphone passages become quieter. Use slower release for smoother room tails.
steps: Source: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

limiter.title: Catch peaks before monitoring
limiter.explanation: Reduce peaks before the headphone feed. Leave output headroom and listen for distortion; this is not a guarantee against downstream clipping.
steps: Source: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

delay.title: Add a rhythmic echo
delay.explanation: 375 ms is a dotted eighth note at 120 BPM. Moderate feedback gives several repeats. Millisecond delay stays fixed when project tempo changes.

reverb.title: Put a voice in a small space
reverb.explanation: Blend a restrained damped reverb into a played voice. Increase Mix carefully to preserve articulation.

overdrive.title: Distort a guitar input
overdrive.explanation: Boost the guitar into the waveshaper, soften the result with Tone, then trim Level before monitoring.
steps: Source: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

granular_pitch_shift.title: Double a live voice an octave up
granular_pitch_shift.explanation: Blend dry microphone audio with a live octave-up granular layer. Grain duration trades response for modulation artifacts.
steps: Source: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

convolution_reverb.title: Color a voice with a recorded response
convolution_reverb.explanation: Choose a room response or noise recording and blend its continuously windowed convolution with the instrument. This implementation is a short-window effect, not an arbitrary long partitioned impulse-response renderer.
steps: Convolution reverb: import or choose a project sample in the modal; sample IDs are specific to your server. Set the sample root note for pitched instruments.

gain.title: Trim an instrument before a shared mix
gain.explanation: Reduce a voice by 12 dB before monitoring. Gain expects dB; insert Amplitude to dB when using a linear envelope.

meter.title: Check microphone headroom
meter.explanation: Read per-channel dBFS peaks before the monitor feed. Level 1 also provides a linear amplitude control for automation or a numeric display.
steps: Source: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

audio_visualizer.title: Inspect the spectrum of a saw voice
audio_visualizer.explanation: The audio passes through unchanged while the node displays block-rate spectral analysis. The documentation preview has no live samples.

pan.title: Move a stereo texture left
pan.explanation: Balance a stereo recording toward the left. Mono is unchanged and channels above two pass through; this is stereo balance, not a mono-to-stereo panner.
steps: Source: import or choose a project sample in the modal; sample IDs are specific to your server. Set the sample root note for pitched instruments.

audio_gate.title: Chop a sustained voice
audio_gate.explanation: A half-Hz LFO crosses zero to open and close the smoothed audio gate. Negative and zero Open values close it.

channel_map.title: Swap left and right
channel_map.explanation: Swap a stereo recording’s channels. Source 0 mutes an output; repeating a source duplicates it.
steps: Source: import or choose a project sample in the modal; sample IDs are specific to your server. Set the sample root note for pitched instruments.

oscillator.title: Check the listening path with a test tone
oscillator.explanation: Route the source through a low Gain and Meter to the listening destination. Enable the engine to run the graph; continuous sources do not need show Play.
steps: These examples use two-channel bundles throughout. Open each modal to match channel widths when recreating the patch.

noise.title: Make a noise source for sound design
noise.explanation: Broadband noise is useful as a percussion or wind source. Begin at a low level, then add filters and an envelope for a shaped sound.
steps: These examples use two-channel bundles throughout. Open each modal to match channel widths when recreating the patch.

sample.title: Loop a recorded ambience
sample.explanation: Route the source through a low Gain and Meter to the listening destination. Enable the engine to run the graph; continuous sources do not need show Play.
steps: These examples use two-channel bundles throughout. Open each modal to match channel widths when recreating the patch.
Sample player: import or choose a project sample in the modal; sample IDs are specific to your server. Set the sample root note for pitched instruments.

For a compact sample palette, add a Sample selector, build its shortlist in options, and connect its Sample ID output to this node’s Sample ID input. Match channel counts; changing the sample stops old playback/voices. The sampler root note remains its configured setting.

phase_vocoder.title: Slow a texture without lowering its pitch
phase_vocoder.explanation: Select a recorded texture. Speed 0.5 stretches playback to twice its duration while Pitch stays at zero semitones. These settings are prepared structural edits.
steps: These examples use two-channel bundles throughout. Open each modal to match channel widths when recreating the patch.
Phase vocoder: import or choose a project sample in the modal; sample IDs are specific to your server. Set the sample root note for pitched instruments.

input.title: Monitor a server-connected instrument
input.explanation: Route the source through a low Gain and Meter to the listening destination. Enable the engine to run the graph; continuous sources do not need show Play.
steps: These examples use two-channel bundles throughout. Open each modal to match channel widths when recreating the patch.
Audio input: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

browser_input.title: Bring a remote performer into the mix
browser_input.explanation: The assigned performer’s microphone travels to the server over WebRTC, then through the graph to this monitor feed. Use headphones to avoid an acoustic loop.
steps: These examples use two-channel bundles throughout. Open each modal to match channel widths when recreating the patch.
Local audio input: assign an ensemble member, choose the input on that member’s device and allow microphone access over HTTPS or localhost.

output.title: Send the mix to server speakers
output.explanation: Route the source through a low Gain and Meter to the listening destination. Enable the engine to run the graph; continuous sources do not need show Play.
steps: These examples use two-channel bundles throughout. Open each modal to match channel widths when recreating the patch.
Enable the server’s output interface in System settings and select its physical channel routes in Audio output. Start with low output gain.

monitor_output.title: Make a dedicated headphone feed
monitor_output.explanation: Select this named Monitor output in the browser monitor and connect it. It is independent of the hardware master; mono duplicates to stereo and wider bundles use the first two channels.
steps: These examples use two-channel bundles throughout. Open each modal to match channel widths when recreating the patch.

mixer.title: Combine two recorded textures
mixer.explanation: Sum two equal-width sources. The default −6 dB mixer gain leaves headroom for their sum.
steps: Texture A: import or choose a project sample in the modal; sample IDs are specific to your server. Set the sample root note for pitched instruments.
Texture B: import or choose a project sample in the modal; sample IDs are specific to your server. Set the sample root note for pitched instruments.

crossfade.title: Transition between two ambiences
crossfade.explanation: Mix 0 selects A; Mix 1 selects B. Move Mix during a scene transition. Equal-power curves can boost correlated material, so leave headroom.
steps: Texture A: import or choose a project sample in the modal; sample IDs are specific to your server. Set the sample root note for pitched instruments.
Texture B: import or choose a project sample in the modal; sample IDs are specific to your server. Set the sample root note for pitched instruments.

vocoder.title: Make a talking synthesizer
vocoder.explanation: A harmonically rich saw supplies the carrier; microphone speech supplies the modulator. Speak while the carrier runs to impose the voice’s band envelopes on the synthetic tone. Both inputs must have equal channel widths.
steps: Voice modulator: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

convolution.title: Cross-synthesize voice and a tone
convolution.explanation: The latest microphone window becomes a changing impulse response applied to the saw source. Enable Normalize and experiment with Window size for granular cross-synthesis; this is not a stored room impulse.
steps: Texture B: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

channel_split.title: Process only the left channel
channel_split.explanation: Split a stereo recording into mono cables, trim the left by 6 dB, and merge it with the untouched right. Split and Merge are two-channel nodes; the Gain between them must be mono.
steps: Stereo field recording: import or choose a project sample in the modal; sample IDs are specific to your server. Set the sample root note for pitched instruments.

channel_merge.title: Process only the left channel
channel_merge.explanation: Split a stereo recording into mono cables, trim the left by 6 dB, and merge it with the untouched right. Split and Merge are two-channel nodes; the Gain between them must be mono.
steps: Stereo field recording: import or choose a project sample in the modal; sample IDs are specific to your server. Set the sample root note for pitched instruments.

audio_to_control.title: Build audio-rate frequency modulation
audio_to_control.explanation: Convert the modulator’s first audio channel to a control signal, multiply by 120 Hz and offset by 440 Hz. It drives carrier Frequency every sample. Actual deviation also depends on modulator Amplitude.

envelope.title: Follow an instrument’s level
envelope.explanation: Measure the input envelope as a linear control for responsive visuals or dynamics. Release smooths the falling level.
steps: Instrument microphone: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

pitch_tracker.title: Inspect sung note estimates
pitch_tracker.explanation: Sing sustained single notes and read the strongest integer MIDI estimate. −1 means no pitch. A larger FFT improves low-note resolution while adding delay; harmonics and noisy attacks can confuse the estimate.
steps: Instrument microphone: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

fft.title: Reshape a recorded spectrum
fft.explanation: Analyze a recorded texture, process its spectral frames, then resynthesize audio for the monitor. Every spectral node uses 1024 samples, overlap 4 and two channels. The frame path adds analysis latency. The magnitude curve leaves the lowest bins at unity and reduces the upper spectrum to 0.25; adjust the curve in the modal.
steps: Recorded texture: import or choose a project sample in the modal; sample IDs are specific to your server. Set the sample root note for pitched instruments.

send_audio.title: Share a named audio route
send_audio.explanation: Set Target name to texture on both Send and Receive. The matching name is the connection between them; there is deliberately no physical cable across that gap. Routes are project-local and add one sample of delay. Match channel width and, for spectral routes, FFT size and overlap. Audio senders mix; spectral receives choose the uppermost compatible sender.

record.title: Archive a live instrument take
record.explanation: Record take and Stop take send positive pulses. The input is written to a timestamped multichannel float WAV in the server recordings folder. The node label becomes the filename prefix. Show Stop leaves recording running; send Stop or disable the engine to finalize it.
steps: Live instrument: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

looper.title: Capture and replay a four-beat phrase
looper.explanation: The buttons emit track number 1 then return to zero. Four-beat loop mode queues recording/playback at the next graph-clock bar. Stop recording is immediate; use Play track 1 to start playback. Re-recording replaces track 1, and playback does not time-stretch with tempo.
steps: Live instrument: enable a physical input in System settings, then choose its interface and channel routes in the node modal.

subgraph.title: Package a reusable audio processor
subgraph.explanation: This is the inside of a subgraph. Named input and output boundary nodes become ports on the parent. Rename them to name the public contract; internal cables process the signal between those boundaries. Save the parent to the subgraph library to reuse a version.
steps: Create the subgraph, open it, then add these boundary and processing nodes inside. Match public channel widths and spectral frame settings to the surrounding patch.

sample_selector.title: Keep a small sample palette for a sampler
sample_selector.explanation: Collect a few samples in one place while developing a patch. Add a kick, snare and hi-hat in the selector options; they become entries 0, 1 and 2. Give them short nicknames such as Kick, Snare and Hat. The orange buttons show those nicknames, and clicking one outputs its numeric Sample ID to the sampler. Connect a number source to Index when the same shortlist should be selected by the graph instead of by hand. Sample selection and note triggering are separate.
steps: In the Samples library, import audio or use Browse all and Add to project. Use samples with the same channel count as the sampler.

Open Sample selector options. Use Find a sample and Add sample to build the ordered list. Edit optional nicknames; use the arrows to reorder entries or Remove to shorten the list. Indices always run from 0 through n−1 (up to 64 entries).
Connect Sample selector / Sample ID to Polyphonic sampler / Sample ID. With no Index cable, click an orange button on the selector to choose a sample during development.
To select by number, connect Input value / Value to the selector Index. Set the Input value to 0, 1 or 2. A connected Index shows the engine value and disables manual sample buttons.

Connect Piano / MIDI to the sampler, choose the sampler root MIDI note and connect its audio to Browser monitor. Enable the engine, connect the monitor and play the Piano. Selecting a different sample stops old voices; play a new note to hear it.

The engine prepares shortlist audio before rendering. The Sample ID input accepts the sampler default and matching-channel samples from graph shortlists. Unknown, unavailable or mismatched IDs select silence. Fractional indices round down; an empty list or an index outside the list outputs 0.

part_player.title: Trigger algorithmic MIDI snippets without starting the show
part_player.explanation: Choose a score part in the Part player Options. In a freeform project, use triggers or an algorithmic graph to launch that snippet at the current performance tempo while the show is stopped. The player sends standard MIDI to an instrument or MIDI output and displays the selected part’s written bar and beat. Each player has its own position.
steps: Create a short score part, including any trailing rests, then select it in the Part player’s Source part menu. Enable the audio engine; the performance can remain stopped.

Connect a Trigger output to Play for one complete pass. A rising positive signal schedules the beginning on the next metronome beat, without count-in. Retriggering starts over at the next beat; existing playback continues until that boundary.

Connect another Trigger to Play & repeat for continuous looping of the entire part. Stop cancels a waiting launch or immediately releases the player’s held notes. If triggers coincide, Stop wins, then Play & repeat. Held positive signals do not repeatedly restart.

Connect the MIDI outlet to MIDI output and choose the destination port in that node’s Options, or connect it to a synth or sampler. The five numeric note outputs also use the standard pitch, velocity, gate, trigger and note-off contract.

Notation repeats, ties, articulation, staff MIDI channels, dynamics and MIDI automation are prepared from the selected part. Authored tempo changes and show count-in do not override the current tempo for this node. Show mute/solo and performer queues do not gate explicit graph playback.

Changing the selected part or its musical content stops the old clip and releases its notes. Moving or renaming a node preserves playback. Enabling physical MIDI devices requires a manual device check.

Click the bar/beat panel to open a read-only playback viewer for this node’s selected part. Toggle Notation or Piano roll; all staves show the node’s own playhead, including notation-repeat jumps. This viewer does not edit notes or control show transport.

granular_cloud.title: Scan a field recording as a continuous grain cloud
granular_cloud.explanation: Granular Cloud creates a continuous texture from randomly placed, overlapping Hann-enveloped slices of one selected sample. It reuses Granular synth’s grain scheduler and controls, with no MIDI inlet. Drive Cloud center from 0 to 1 to move through the sample; Spray scatters grain starts around that point.
steps: Choose or import a sample in Options and enable the audio engine. With no Gate, Trigger or note-off connections, the cloud runs continuously even while show transport is stopped. Amplitude controls its overall level.

Connect the Center value output to Cloud center (the position port). Values are normalized: 0 is the sample start and 1 is its end. Random starts and grain playback wrap around the sample edges. Changes affect newly launched grains.
Adjust Spray (milliseconds around the center), Grain duration and Density (grains per second per held voice) to shape the texture. Each grain uses the same smooth Hann window as Granular synth.

The synth’s numeric Pitch, Velocity, Gate, Trigger, note-off, root note, sample ID, amplitude and release controls remain available. Optional Pitch/Velocity inputs set the continuous voice. Wiring Gate or Trigger/note-off switches to the synth’s numeric note control; pair trigger and note-off with pitch for independent note releases. No MIDI cable can connect directly.
Connect Sample selector to Sample ID for live source selection. Samples are prepared outside rendering; the fixed 16-voice/128-grain pool and existing sample-memory limits apply.
